results.name: above_below_asym_max_last
results.description: In sets of >=2 whose largest example is shown last, yes-rate for targets 1-10 above the max minus yes-rate for targets 1-10 below the min; observed below null means people extend upward even less (the model under-credits the top edge), above null means the model over-sharpens the top edge.
results.code:
# name: above_below_asym_max_last
# description: In sets of >=2 whose largest example is shown last, yes-rate for targets 1-10 above the max minus yes-rate for targets 1-10 below the min; observed below null means people extend upward even less (the model under-credits the top edge), above null means the model over-sharpens the top edge.
def test_statistic(df):
    sp = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",")
    n = sp.str.len().values
    last = sp.str[-1].astype(int).values
    mx = sp.apply(lambda v: max(int(x) for x in v)).values
    mn = sp.apply(lambda v: min(int(x) for x in v)).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    g = (n >= 2) & (last == mx)
    up = g & (t > mx) & (t <= mx + 10)
    dn = g & (t < mn) & (t >= mn - 10)
    if up.sum() == 0 or dn.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[up].mean() - r[dn].mean())

results.name: last_vs_earlier_example_yes
results.description: Yes-rate when the target is the LAST-shown example minus yes-rate when it is an earlier-shown example (sets of >=2); observed below null means people reject the final example more than the model (which treats all examples alike, or favours a last max) predicts.
results.code:
# name: last_vs_earlier_example_yes
# description: Yes-rate when the target is the LAST-shown example minus yes-rate when it is an earlier-shown example (sets of >=2); observed below null means people reject the final example more than the model (which treats all examples alike, or favours a last max) predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False)
    n = sets.str.count(",") + 1
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    last = sets.str.split(",").str[-1].astype(int).values
    padded = ("," + sets + ",").values
    is_ex = np.array([("," + str(a) + ",") in b for a, b in zip(t, padded)])
    multi = (n >= 2).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    a = multi & is_ex & (t == last)
    b = multi & is_ex & (t != last)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: below_above_asym_min_last
results.description: In sets of >=2 whose smallest example is shown last, yes-rate for targets 1-10 below the min minus yes-rate for targets 1-10 above the max; observed below null means a last-shown minimum also marks a sharp lower edge, which the model (edge credit only for a last max) misses.

results.name: example_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate among trials whose target is one of the shown examples (sets of >=2); observed below null means the model over-produces "yes" to the examples themselves (people sometimes reject a shown example).
results.code:
# name: example_target_yes_rate
# description: Yes-rate among trials whose target is one of the shown examples (sets of >=2); observed below null means the model over-produces "yes" to the examples themselves (people sometimes reject a shown example).
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    n = sets.str.count(",") + 1
    t = df["target"].astype(int).astype(str)
    padded = "," + sets.str.replace(" ", "", regex=False) + ","
    is_ex = pd.Series([("," + a + ",") in b for a, b in zip(t.values, padded.values)], index=df.index)
    m = is_ex & (n >= 2)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df.loc[m, "rating"].astype(float).mean())

results.name: session_yes_rate_sd
results.description: SD across sessions (split where trial_index resets) of the per-session yes-rate; observed above null means between-participant differences in overall yes-bias exceed what the single-population model produces.
results.code:
# name: session_yes_rate_sd
# description: SD across sessions (split where trial_index resets) of the per-session yes-rate; observed above null means between-participant differences in overall yes-bias exceed what the single-population model produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(int).values
    sess = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(np.diff(ti) < 0)])
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    m = pd.Series(r).groupby(sess).mean()
    return float(m.std(ddof=0)) if len(m) > 1 else 0.0

results.name: singleton_near_generalization
results.description: For single-example sets, yes-rate to non-example targets within 10 of the example; observed above null means people generalise to neighbours of a lone example more broadly than the model predicts, below null means less.
results.code:
# name: singleton_near_generalization
# description: For single-example sets, yes-rate to non-example targets within 10 of the example; observed above null means people generalise to neighbours of a lone example more broadly than the model predicts, below null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False)
    single = ~s.str.contains(",")
    x = pd.to_numeric(s.where(single, "0"), errors="coerce").fillna(0).astype(int).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    d = np.abs(t - x)
    m = single.values & (d >= 1) & (d <= 10)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].astype(float).values[m].mean())

results.name: interior_proximity_corr
results.description: Among non-example targets strictly between the min and max of sets of >=2 (span >= 10), the correlation of rating with distance to the nearest example divided by span; observed more negative than null means people's yes falls off with distance from examples inside the range, which uniform-range concepts underproduce.

results.name: rule_breaking_example_yes_gap
results.description: For sets of >=3, yes-rate to a shown example that violates a simple rule (multiple of k, last digit, powers, squares, primes, parity) shared by all the other examples, minus yes-rate to the other shown examples; observed more negative than null means people discount outlier examples more than the model's 10% noise allows.
